Interface Fetchable

All Known Subinterfaces:
Query.Compiled.Connected, Query.Connected.Compiled, Query.Connected.Constant, Query.Constant.Connected
All Known Implementing Classes:
Command, Cursor
public interface Fetchable
Object that can fetch query results in different formats.

    • fetchMapPage

      default Page<Map<String,Object>> fetchMapPage(int pageSize, int pageIndx)
      Fetches the current result set as a Page of maps whose keys are the column names and values are the column values.

      The query must include a dataSize column containing the total number of rows that match the filter, ignoring pagination. The usual way to provide it is with a window function such as count(*) over() as dataSize.

      This method does not issue a separate count(*) query. It only consumes the current result set.

      Parameters:
      pageSize - number of rows per page
      pageIndx - index of the page
      Returns:
      a page containing the current rows and the total size informed by dataSize
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the result set does not contain a dataSize column

    • fetchMapPage

      default Page<Map<String,Object>> fetchMapPage(int pageSize, int pageIndx, Class<?>... types)
      Fetches the current result set as a Page of typed maps.

      The query must include a dataSize column containing the total number of rows that match the filter, ignoring pagination. The usual way to provide it is with a window function such as count(*) over() as dataSize.

      This method does not issue a separate count(*) query. It only consumes the current result set and maps each non-dataSize column using the corresponding entry from types.

      Parameters:
      pageSize - number of rows per page
      pageIndx - index of the page
      types - types of the objects to be fetched for each non-dataSize column
      Returns:
      a page containing the current rows and the total size informed by dataSize
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the result set does not contain a dataSize column

    • fetchEntity

      default <T> Optional<T> fetchEntity(Class<T> type, Function<String,Object> context)
      Fetches the first row as a Java object of the specified type, allowing contextual values to be supplied for specific properties before they are read from the result set.

      The context may provide a value for a property, identified by its full name, before the cursor tries to read it from the current row. Returning null means the property should be resolved normally from the cursor.

      Parameters:
      type - type of the object to be fetched
      context - function used to provide contextual values for specific property names
      Returns:
      an Optional describing the first row of the result as a Java object of the specified type

    • fetchEntityPage

      default <T> Page<T> fetchEntityPage(Class<T> type, int pageSize, int pageIndx)
      Fetches the current result set as a Page of Java objects of the specified type.

      The query must include a dataSize column containing the total number of rows that match the filter, ignoring pagination. The usual way to provide it is with a window function such as count(*) over() as dataSize.

      This method does not issue a separate count(*) query. It only consumes the current result set and materializes each row using the same entity construction rules used by the rest of the framework.

      Parameters:
      type - type of the objects to be fetched
      pageSize - number of entities per page
      pageIndx - index of the page
      Returns:
      a page containing the current rows and the total size informed by dataSize
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the result set does not contain a dataSize column

    • fetchEntityPage

      default <T> Page<T> fetchEntityPage(Class<T> type, int pageSize, int pageIndx, Function<String,Object> context)
      Fetches the current result set as a Page of Java objects of the specified type, allowing contextual values to be supplied for specific properties before they are read from the result set.

      The query must include a dataSize column containing the total number of rows that match the filter, ignoring pagination. The usual way to provide it is with a window function such as count(*) over() as dataSize.

      The context may provide a value for a property, identified by its full name, before the cursor tries to read it from the current row. Returning null means the property should be resolved normally from the cursor.

      Parameters:
      type - type of the objects to be fetched
      pageSize - number of entities per page
      pageIndx - index of the page
      context - function used to provide contextual values for specific property names
      Returns:
      a page containing the current rows and the total size informed by dataSize
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the result set does not contain a dataSize column
